 Eternal’s Deepinder Goyal unveils Dark.ai, his new bet on AI
 The upcoming AI initiative marks another technology push by the Zomato and Blinkit parent, though details of its features, target users and business model remain limited.

Deepinder Goyal , founder of Zomato and Vice-Chairman of its parent company Eternal , has teased a new artificial intelligence (AI) initiative called Dark.ai , adding to the company’s technology ambitions beyond its core food delivery and quick commerce businesses.
 “Dark.ai – from the house of Eternal. Coming soon,” Goyal wrote in a post on X on Wednesday, October 21. The post featured a photograph of a desktop monitor and laptop displaying the words “DARK BY ETERNAL”.
 Advt 
 New venture on radar 
While Goyal’s post offered little information about the upcoming initiative, the branding has raised questions about whether Dark.ai will be a standalone AI product, a consumer-facing service or a technology platform aimed at businesses.
 Eternal has not yet detailed the product’s features, target audience, pricing or revenue model. It is also unclear how the initiative will connect with the company’s existing portfolio, which includes Zomato, Blinkit, Hyperpure and District.
The teaser follows Goyal’s growing interest in ventures beyond Eternal’s established businesses. Since stepping down as group CEO and MD in February 2026, he has pursued other technology-led initiatives, including Temple, a brain-health wearable, and Continue Research, a longevity-focused initiative. He has also co-founded aviation startup LAT Aerospace.
 Goyal had earlier indicated that he wanted to explore ideas involving greater risk-taking and experimentation outside a publicly listed company. In that context, the Dark.ai announcement raises questions about how the new initiative fits into Eternal’s broader strategy.
The company has also been exploring the role of AI in its existing operations. In April, Goyal said AI chat interfaces were not yet close to disrupting Eternal’s businesses, arguing that technology could support growth but could not independently handle physical operations such as food delivery through traffic or stocking dark stores.
 Advt 
 Further details about Dark.ai are expected to clarify the product’s intended use and its place in Eternal’s expanding technology portfolio.
